new_results.statement: If AU=U Lambda, U has r orthonormal genuine eigenvectors with min |lambda|>=a, and H is a physical set of size h<r, then for C=A[H^c,H^c], s_{r-h}(C)>=a sqrt(1-||U_H^T U_H||op).

For a selected-three eigframe and physical coordinate i with row leverage p, writing b=A[-i,i] and C=A[-i,-i], s3(C)>=[L sqrt(1-p)-||b|| sqrt(p)]_+. Under p<=1/48, either ||b||>L/4 or s3(C)>=0.953444115428808 L.

The full one-scale spectral window either pays the ambient form continuously by <64/L, or a high-window physical coordinate leaves a three-direction child at L/(64sqrt3) unless it is ultra-high; the child window either pays the original ambient form by <7013/L or produces a second physical high-window coordinate.

partner_applied.actual_use: Partner k=1 high-top-two-leverage branch supplies an original cross-row g with ||g||>(3/16)sqrt(3/10)L=0.102697979532218L. At the same coordinate, the new row-defect theorem forces either a full star >L/4 or a principal child with s3>=0.953444115428808L. On the latter branch, the ambient child ridge theorem pays the original full form by <67/L with continuous C0 density when the child window is diffuse; otherwise a distinct child coordinate has scalar/star >0.00186219553795L.

collective_tail_applied.actual_use: Under the current partner k=1 collective-tail hypotheses, gives continuous density <584/L, so the star/core router treats a genuine survivor after this diffuse exit.
